# repo_info

What the store is and holds: its id and name, the changeset main points at, and how many changesets and refs it has.

```yaml
title: "repo_info"
description: "Describe the store."
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: false
identity_required: false
cli_command: "swarmops info"
envelope_op: "repo_info"
request_type: "InfoReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `InfoReq`: `swarmops schema InfoReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

It takes no fields: pass `{}`.

### JSON Schema

As `tools/list` gives it: each `$ref` replaced by its definition, so that it stands alone.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "`info`: describe the store. It has no options yet.",
  "title": "InfoReq",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## Annotations

It only reads the store.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `true` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops info`](../commands/info.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Examples

### MCP

```json
{
  "id": 2,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "arguments": {},
    "name": "repo_info"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "id": 2,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "text": "{\"ok\":true,\"op\":\"repo_info\",\"api\":1,\"result\":{\"repo_id\":\"[repo_id]\",\"name\":\"store\",\"store_version\":1,\"changesets\":0,\"refs\":0},\"meta\":{\"repo\":\"[tmp]/store\",\"elapsed_ms\":\"[elapsed_ms]\",\"resolved\":{},\"auth\":\"trust\"}}",
        "type": "text"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false,
    "structuredContent": {
      "api": 1,
      "meta": {
        "auth": "trust",
        "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
        "repo": "[tmp]/store",
        "resolved": {}
      },
      "ok": true,
      "op": "repo_info",
      "result": {
        "changesets": 0,
        "name": "store",
        "refs": 0,
        "repo_id": "[repo_id]",
        "store_version": 1
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `repo_info`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops info`](../commands/info.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `InfoReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops info`](../commands/info.md#errors) lists them.
